result.title: DANGERLENS: Probing Dangerous Representations Hidden by Safety Alignment
result.summary: Safety alignment teaches language models to refuse harmful requests, yet the internal accessibility of hazardous concepts can retain traces of earlier training. Can checkpoints with equally safe behavior differ in what remains accessible behind their refusals? In this work, we investigate this question through paired training histories and a direct audit of intermediate representations. We introduce DANGERLENS, a probe that maps hidden states into vocabulary space and uses blinded semantic judgments to distinguish harmful goals and operational means from hazard recognition and safety control. Experiments on three Qwen1.5 scales show that checkpoints with prior harmful exposure generally retain greater hazardous concept accessibility after the same safety alignment, with the strongest separation in intermediate and later layers. The same harmful update also produces different behavioral trajectories from closely matched starting points. Human relevance validation and readout ablations reinforce the measured accessibility contrast. Our findings show that training history remains visible inside behaviorally matched models and motivate internal accessibility audits alongside output safety evaluations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用成对训练历史与中间表示审计，提出 DANGERLENS 探针把隐状态映射到词表空间并结合盲评，区分有害目标与安全控制信息，发现行为同样安全的模型在内部有害概念可及性上仍存在差异，且差异集中在中间与较后层。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「隐状态探针＋readout 消融」评估中间层可及性的做法，或可迁移用于核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正保留任务必要的视觉证据；但研究属安全对齐领域，与多模态推理无直接关联，借鉴价值待人工核查。
